prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a coarse room layout: the floor extends forward to a wall and doorway, while bright foreground regions at the bottom and side edges are nearest and the dark upper wall and doorway are farther away. Across the five frames, the dog is roughly 1–2 m in front of the camera wearer, moving from partly cut off at the bottom to more fully visible near the lower centre-right; the walls and doorway appear roughly 2–4 m away. The nearest bottom-edge objects and, in later frames, the right wall edge may be within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach, while the dog does not clearly enter arm’s reach; no person is visible, so facing direction, gaze, and interpersonal distance cannot be established. Compared with RGB, the map makes foreground-versus-background separation and the camera’s rightward turn clearer, but it is unreliable at image borders, on the dog, and around the bright rectangular foreground object, and its grayscale values do not provide calibrated metric distances.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates only a few regions against black: a large upper-middle region labelled refrigerator in frame 2, small dog and bird regions near the lower middle in frame 3, a dog and a toilet region in frame 4, and toilet plus large blue regions near the right edge in frame 5. In RGB context, the dog is about 1–2 m ahead and shifts from partly below the frame to the lower centre-right as the camera turns right; the other labelled masks do not reliably correspond to the visible room objects, so their distances and mutual spacing cannot be trusted. The dog masks clarify its silhouette, partial occlusion by the lower frame boundary, and left/right position, but they do not establish whether it faces or looks toward the camera wearer, and no people or body parts are segmented. The map is highly unreliable here because detections appear and disappear between adjacent frames, the bird and toilet labels are implausible in the RGB scene, much of the room is unlabelled, and several objects remain partly outside the image.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black in all five frames, so it supplies no detected body or hand skeletons and therefore no usable information about people, facing direction, gaze, limb position, reach, or interpersonal spacing. In RGB context, no person is clearly visible; the main moving subject is a dog roughly 1–2 m in front of the camera wearer, which this human-pose representation does not capture. The blank result also cannot describe the room layout, object distances, occlusions, or the camera’s rightward turn across the sequence. Its only spatially relevant indication is that no human pose was detected, but this is not proof that no person or hand is present because partial, occluded, or out-of-frame bodies could be missed.
